statement.p: Calculate the Taylor polynomials T_2(x) and T_3(x) centered at x = \frac{\pi }{6} for f(x) = \sin\mathopen{}\left(x\right).

static.solution:
\begin{array}{lcll} T(x) \amp = \amp \amp f(a) \cr\cr \amp \amp + \amp \frac{f'(a)}{1!} (x-a) \cr \cr \amp \amp + \amp \frac{f''(a)}{2!} (x-a)^2 \cr \cr \amp \amp + \amp \ldots \cr \cr \amp \amp + \amp \frac{f^n(a)}{n!} (x-a)^n \end{array}
So, in this case, f(x) = \sin\mathopen{}\left(x\right) and
T_2(x) = A + B(x-\frac{\pi }{6}) + C(x-\frac{\pi }{6})^2
where
A=f(\frac{\pi }{6})=\frac{1}{2}=0.5
B=f'(\frac{\pi }{6})=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}=0.866025403784439
C=\frac{f''(\frac{\pi }{6})}{2!}=-\frac{1}{4}=-0.25
Thus,
T_2(x) = \frac{1}{2} + \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} (x - \frac{\pi }{6}) - \frac{1}{4} (x - \frac{\pi }{6})^2
or
T_2(x) = 0.5+0.866025\mathopen{}\left(x-\frac{\pi }{6}\right)-0.25\mathopen{}\left(x-\frac{\pi }{6}\right)^{2}
Similarly,
T_3(x) = D + E(x-\frac{\pi }{6}) + F(x-\frac{\pi }{6})^2 + G(x-\frac{\pi }{6})^3
where
D=f(\frac{\pi }{6})=\frac{1}{2} = 0.5
E=f'(\frac{\pi }{6})=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} =0.866025403784439
F=\frac{f''(\frac{\pi }{6})}{2!}=-\frac{1}{4} =-0.25
G=\frac{f'''(\frac{\pi }{6})}{3!}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{12}=-0.144337567297406
Thus, T_3(x) = \frac{1}{2} + \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} (x - \frac{\pi }{6}) - \frac{1}{4} (x - \frac{\pi }{6})^2 + \frac{\sqrt{3}}{12} (x - \frac{\pi }{6})^3
or
T_3(x) = 0.5+0.866025\mathopen{}\left(x-\frac{\pi }{6}\right)-0.25\mathopen{}\left(x-\frac{\pi }{6}\right)^{2}-0.144338\mathopen{}\left(x-\frac{\pi }{6}\right)^{3}
